sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.

sentences.en: The charges stem from Castro's role in a decades-old incident when three Americans were killed by the Cuban government.

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Frances Robles on the story behind the charges against Castro and Julian Barnes on what the American government really wants from Cuba.

sentences.en: I've been covering judicial events and press conferences and court cases and announcements for many, many years.

sentences.en: And I can't say I've ever seen one quite like this.

sentences.en: It's kind of a cool, old-looking tower.

sentences.en: And the reason it's an important location is because in the 1960s and the early 70s, it was the Cuban Refugee Center.
sentences.zh: 它之所以是一个重要的地点，是因为在20世纪60年代和70年代初，它是古巴难民中心。

sentences.en: So it's basically Ellis Island for Cuban exiles.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上就是古巴流亡者的埃利斯岛。

sentences.en: It was the first stop for many, many thousands of people who left Cuba after the revolution and came to live in Miami.
sentences.zh: 对于成千上万在革命后离开古巴并来到迈阿密生活的人来说，这是他们的第一站。

sentences.en: So a lot of symbolism there for people.

sentences.en: I was kind of struck, to be honest, that the first speaker was Madeline Pumariega, who's a Cuban-American woman, the president of Miami-Dade College.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我有点惊讶，第一位发言人是马德琳·普马列加，她是一位古巴裔美国女性，也是迈阿密戴德学院的院长。

sentences.en: The building that we were in is part of Miami-Dade College.
sentences.zh: 我们所在的建筑是迈阿密戴德学院的一部分。

sentences.en: And so it was interesting to me because she's a very prominent member of the community, but she's not a prosecutor.

sentences.en: So it told you a lot.

sentences.en: This is a community event.

sentences.en: And to our brothers and sisters in Cuba, we hear you.

sentences.en: The hundreds of people in the room got up and gave him a standing ovation before the man even opened his mouth.

sentences.en: Thank you very much.

sentences.en: Yeah, he got right into it.

sentences.en: Today, we are announcing an indictment charging Raul Castro and several others with conspiracy to kill U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们宣布起诉劳尔·卡斯特罗及其他几人，罪名是密谋杀害美国

sentences.en: nationals.

sentences.en: nationals.

sentences.en: And he just started reading out the charges.

sentences.zh: 卡斯特罗先生和其他人还被指控犯有其他罪行，包括破坏飞机和四项个人谋杀罪。

sentences.en: He was being charged with conspiracy to kill U.S.

sentences.zh: 他们所说的谋杀事件是指哪一起？

sentences.zh: 这个案件所涉及的事件发生在1996年。

sentences.en: But really, to tell that story, I'm going to go back further.
sentences.zh: 但为了讲好这个故事，我得追溯得更远一点。

sentences.en: I'm going to go a little early in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 我要回到90年代初。

sentences.en: There was a point in the 90s where Cubans were literally throwing themselves to the sea to make it to the United States.
sentences.zh: 90年代有段时间，古巴人真的在把自己投向大海，试图到达美国。

sentences.en: They were doing that on inner tubes.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在内胎上这样做。

sentences.en: They were doing that on old cars that they rebuilt into a boat on rafts.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在用旧车改装成的船或木筏上这样做。

sentences.en: And so it becomes what's known as the Cuban Rafter Crisis, because there's so many people, literally
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的古巴木筏危机，因为有太多人，真的是

sentences.en: thousands and thousands of people that were in the sea trying to make it to the United States.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人在海上试图到达美国。

sentences.en: And so with that crisis is born an organization called Brothers to the Rescue.
sentences.zh: 随着这场危机，一个名为“救援兄弟会”的组织诞生了。

sentences.en: And what they were doing, they were Cuban-American pilots who raised money to buy small planes, and they would fly over the Straits of Florida between the Florida Keys and Cuba.
sentences.zh: 他们是古巴裔美国飞行员，筹集资金购买小型飞机，在佛罗里达群岛和古巴之间的佛罗里达海峡上空飞行。

sentences.en: And it's where many, many people died trying to make their way to the United States.
sentences.zh: 那是许多人在试图前往美国途中丧生的地方。

sentences.en: So they would fly over the waters and they would spot somebody, you know, on a raft, in an inner tube, what have you, and they would call the Coast Guard for help.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会在水面上空飞行，如果发现有人在木筏上、内胎里什么的，他们就会呼叫海岸警卫队寻求帮助。

sentences.en: So this is a nonprofit organization that is attempting to help these people that are migrating en masse from Cuba.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非营利组织，试图帮助那些从古巴大规模移民的人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: They saved hundreds, if not thousands, of people.
sentences.zh: 他们拯救了数百甚至数千人。

sentences.en: They did over 2,000 flights.
sentences.zh: 他们执行了超过2000次飞行任务。

sentences.en: It was a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这可是件大事。

sentences.en: The Coast Guard was overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 海岸警卫队当时不堪重负。

sentences.en: The Coast Guard couldn't handle the volume.
sentences.zh: 海岸警卫队无法处理那么大的流量。

sentences.en: There was a point in the summer of 1994, Natalie, this is a true story, where there were about 2,000 people a day were showing up in Key WeSt.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，1994年夏天有段时间，这是一个真实的故事，每天大约有2000人出现在基韦斯特。

sentences.en: Crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So, why do I start with that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我为什么要从这里开始讲呢？

sentences.en: So the reason that's important is because at some point, the situation gets so dire that the Clinton administration and the Cuban government reach an accord.
sentences.zh: 之所以重要，是因为在某个时刻，局势变得如此严峻，以至于克林顿政府和古巴政府达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: People will try to prevent people from leaving the island, and the United States agrees that when people are caught, they're going to be turned back.
sentences.zh: 人们会试图阻止人们离开该岛，而美国同意当人们被抓获时，他们将被遣返。

sentences.en: And so what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means that the Brothers to the Rescue kind of no longer has a mission.
sentences.zh: 这意味着“救援兄弟会”似乎不再有使命了。

sentences.en: So they change their mission.
sentences.zh: 所以他们改变了使命。

sentences.en: And they start getting a little bit more provocative and poking a stick in the eye of Fidel Castro.
sentences.zh: 他们开始变得更具挑衅性，去戳菲德尔·卡斯特罗的痛处。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: They started dropping leaflets over Cuba.
sentences.zh: 他们开始在古巴上空散发传单。

sentences.en: They dropped religious medallions.
sentences.zh: 他们投下宗教奖章。

sentences.en: Doing things like that, there were a little bit more protest actions as opposed to rescue missions.
sentences.zh: 做这类事情，这更像是抗议行动，而不是救援任务。

sentences.en: The Cuban government was furious.
sentences.zh: 古巴政府非常愤怒。

sentences.en: They felt like this was an illegal incursion into their airspace.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是对其领空的非法入侵。

sentences.en: They kept on turning to the Clinton administration, saying, you guys got to put a stop to this.
sentences.zh: 他们不断向克林顿政府施压，说你们必须阻止这种行为。

sentences.en: Everybody and their mother warns the organization, you got to stop.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在警告这个组织，你们必须停止。

sentences.en: This is going to blow up in your face.
sentences.zh: 这会给你们带来大麻烦的。

sentences.en: And the founder of the organization was a man named Jose Basulto.
sentences.zh: 该组织的创始人是一个名叫何塞·巴苏尔托的人。

sentences.en: He felt really strongly that this was his right.
sentences.zh: 他非常坚定地认为这是他的权利。

sentences.en: This was his right as a Cuban, as a Cuban-American.
sentences.zh: 这是他作为古巴人、作为古巴裔美国人的权利。

sentences.en: And he was going to continue those flights.
sentences.zh: 他打算继续这些飞行。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 他也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And what happened?

sentences.en: So one day, February 24, 1996, he left an airport outside of Miami.
sentences.zh: 有一天，1996年2月24日，他从迈阿密外的一个机场起飞。

sentences.en: He and two other planes left.
sentences.zh: 他和另外两架飞机一起离开了。

sentences.en: And they fly down to Cuba.
sentences.zh: 他们飞向古巴。

sentences.en: That day, they did cross what's known as the 24th parallel.
sentences.zh: 那天，他们确实越过了所谓的北纬24度线。

sentences.en: It's international airspace.
sentences.zh: 那是国际空域。

sentences.en: But to the Cubans, they shouldn't have been there.
sentences.zh: 但对古巴人来说，他们本不应该出现在那里。

sentences.en: And so the Cubans on air traffic, they're on air traffic control.
sentences.zh: 所以古巴的空中交通管制部门介入了。

sentences.en: And Jose Basulto, who's the founder of Brothers to the Rescue, as he's supposed to, he announces himself to the air traffic control.
sentences.zh: 而“救援兄弟会”的创始人何塞·巴苏尔托，按照规定，向空中交通管制部门通报了自己的身份。

sentences.en: And he says, good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 他说，下午好。

sentences.en: This is Jose Basulto from Brothers to the Rescue.
sentences.zh: 我是来自“救援兄弟会”的何塞·巴苏尔托。

sentences.en: You know, it's a beautiful day up in the skies above Havana.
sentences.zh: 你知道，哈瓦那上空的天气真好。

sentences.en: And the Cuban air traffic control responds to him saying, you know, if you're below the 24th parallel, that's an activated zone.
sentences.zh: 古巴空中交通管制部门回应他说，你知道，如果你在北纬24度线以下，那就是一个激活区。

sentences.en: That was the word that they used.
sentences.zh: 那是他们用的词。

sentences.en: And he says, this is my right as a free Cuban.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是我作为一个自由古巴人的权利。

sentences.en: And they continue their journey.

sentences.zh: 于是古巴政府、古巴军方将两架飞机从空中击落，造成四人死亡，其中包括三名美国

sentences.en: citizens.

sentences.zh: 我甚至无法向你描述整个南佛罗里达感到的那种震惊。

sentences.en: You were covering this at the time, right, Frenchie?
sentences.zh: 你当时在报道这件事，对吧，弗兰奇？

sentences.zh: 我确实参加了。

sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友想去橙色碗体育场参加追悼会，那是一个我们过去常去的大型足球场。

sentences.zh: 阿曼多·亚历杭德雷！

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this ties to Raul Castro because I assume this is when he's Secretary of Defense.
sentences.zh: 这与劳尔·卡斯特罗有关，因为我假设那是他担任国防部长的时候。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: He was the defense minister and he gave the order.
sentences.zh: 他当时是国防部长，是他下达的命令。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I don't think that there's too much doubt about that because big pilots in Cuba are not going to be shooting planes out of the sky without very clear chain of commands orders.
sentences.zh: 我认为对此没什么好怀疑的，因为古巴的高级飞行员不可能在没有明确指挥链命令的情况下，就把飞机从天上打下来。

sentences.en: And just explain why, if it was so clear, didn't the U.S.
sentences.zh: 能不能解释一下，如果情况这么明确，为什么美国当时没有

sentences.en: bring charges against him then?
sentences.zh: 对他提起指控？

sentences.en: I've asked that same question to a number of former federal prosecutors.
sentences.zh: 我曾向几位前联邦检察官问过同样的问题。

sentences.en: And the sense that I got was it would just be really destabilizing to diplomatic relations, even though we didn't really have any, and destabilizing in the region.
sentences.zh: 我得到的反馈是，这会严重破坏外交关系——尽管我们当时几乎没什么外交关系——而且会破坏该地区的稳定。

sentences.en: Okay, obviously now there is the political will to indict Raul Castro, who we should say is a 94-year-old man.
sentences.zh: 好的，显然现在有政治意愿去起诉劳尔·卡斯特罗，我们应该说，他已经是一位94岁的老人了。

sentences.en: He was once the president of Cuba, but he's not anymore.
sentences.zh: 他曾经是古巴总统，但现在不是了。

sentences.en: But what you're saying is that targeting him is part of what you've already told us the last time you came on the show,
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，针对他也是你上次上节目时告诉我们的内容的一部分，

sentences.en: which is there has been this escalating pressure campaign by the Trump administration on the Cuban regime.
sentences.zh: 也就是特朗普政府一直在对古巴政权进行升级的施压行动。

sentences.en: You see this as another step in that.
sentences.zh: 你认为这是其中的又一步。

sentences.en: Absolutely, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: I do see this as the latest step in that escalating campaign.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是那场升级行动中的最新一步。

sentences.en: The Trump administration cut off oil to Cuba.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府切断了对古巴的石油供应。

sentences.en: Last week they announced they don't have any reserves left.
sentences.zh: 上周他们宣布古巴已经没有任何储备了。

sentences.en: That means places like Havana are going 22 hours a day without electricity.
sentences.zh: 这意味着像哈瓦那这样的地方每天要停电22个小时。

sentences.en: We keep asking people, what's it like when the power goes out that long?
sentences.zh: 我们一直在问人们，停电这么久是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And I've gotten a very similar answer several times.
sentences.zh: 我好几次得到了非常相似的回答。

sentences.en: No, no, no, it's not when the power goes out that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，问题不在于停电的时候。

sentences.en: It's when the power comes on because the power comes on at maybe 11 o'clock at night or 12 o'clock and you've got to jump out of bed and you have to charge your phone,
sentences.zh: 而在于来电的时候，因为电可能在晚上11点或12点才来，你得从床上跳起来去给手机充电，

sentences.en: you have to charge your laptop.
sentences.zh: 你得给笔记本电脑充电。

sentences.en: And if you're a family ahead of a household, you're getting a pot of rice and beans on the stove to cook the next day's meals.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一家之主，你还得在炉子上煮一锅米饭和豆子，准备第二天的饭菜。

sentences.en: You're hearing really, really dramatic stories like that.
sentences.zh: 你听到的都是非常、非常戏剧性的故事。

sentences.en: People having to walk hours and hours to their jobs.
sentences.zh: 人们不得不步行好几个小时去上班。

sentences.en: People were not able to work because their work depends on having electricity and having Internet.
sentences.zh: 人们无法工作，因为他们的工作依赖于电力和互联网。

sentences.en: It's a really terrible situation.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个可怕的境况。

sentences.en: And when you talk to Cubans on the island, who do they blame for this?
sentences.zh: 当你和岛上的古巴人交谈时，他们把这归咎于谁？

sentences.en: Do they blame the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们是怪美国，

sentences.en: or their own government?
sentences.zh: 还是怪他们自己的政府？

sentences.en: I would say that the answer to that tends to be generational.
sentences.zh: 我会说答案往往取决于代际。

sentences.en: I think older people are blaming the United States.
sentences.zh: 我认为老一辈人会责怪美国。

sentences.en: You know, the talking points from the government is certainly that this is all the United States is for.
sentences.zh: 你知道，政府的宣传口径当然是这一切都是美国的错。

sentences.en: And the younger people are much more apt to blame the Cuban government and for the mistakes that it's made during the management of its country that led to this fiasco.
sentences.zh: 而年轻人则更容易责怪古巴政府，责怪它在管理国家时犯下的错误导致了这场惨剧。

sentences.en: OK, and what about the reaction inside of the Cuban government?
sentences.zh: 好的，那古巴政府内部的反应如何？

sentences.en: What are they saying about this vice grip that the Trump administration has on them?
sentences.zh: 他们对于特朗普政府施加的这种高压手段有什么说法？

sentences.en: They say it's an illegal, I think they've used the word genocide, that it's going to lead to a bloodbath and that it will be the United States' fault.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是非法的，我想他们用了“种族灭绝”这个词，说这会导致血流成河，而且这会是美国的错。

sentences.en: They don't recognize any errors that they've ever made.
sentences.zh: 他们从不承认自己犯过任何错误。

sentences.en: And they 100 percent see this as the fault of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 而且他们百分之百认为这是特朗普政府的错。

sentences.en: And this is a group of people who are used to weathering hard times and still holding on to power, kind of fighting through.
sentences.zh: 这是一群习惯了熬过艰难时期并继续掌权的人，他们算是硬撑过来的。

sentences.en: And it sounds like they're still doing that.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们还在这样做。

sentences.en: It's been 67 years and they have had really severe hardship in the past and they've always weathered.
sentences.zh: 已经67年了，他们过去经历过非常严重的困难，但他们总是能挺过来。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people feel that maybe the Trump administration is underestimating the degree to which these people will want to hang on to power at any coSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很多人觉得，特朗普政府可能低估了这些人不惜一切代价想要保住权力的程度。

sentences.en: After the break, my colleague Julian Barnes takes us inside the U.S.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我的同事朱利安·巴恩斯将带我们深入了解美国

sentences.en: government's broader strategy in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 政府在古巴的更广泛战略。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试着捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Julian, you cover the U.S.
sentences.zh: 朱利安，你负责报道美国

sentences.en: intelligence community and you've been reporting on this pressure campaign and the role of the CIA in amping that up.
sentences.zh: 情报界，你一直在报道这场施压行动以及中央情报局在其中起到的推波助澜的作用。

sentences.en: So just tell us what you've learned.
sentences.zh: 所以，告诉我们你了解到了什么。

sentences.en: What is the endgame in Cuba?
sentences.zh: 古巴的最终目标是什么？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know what the exact endgame is here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不知道这里的确切最终目标是什么。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道美国到底

sentences.en: wants.
sentences.zh: 想要什么。

sentences.en: But what's clear is that the pressure is only going to increase.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，压力只会越来越大。

sentences.en: This indictment is just the next step in that, right?
sentences.zh: 这份起诉书只是其中的下一步，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it is a message to the Cuban government that what happened in Venezuela could happen in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 就像是在向古巴政府传递一个信息：发生在委内瑞拉的事情也可能发生在古巴。

sentences.en: Just want to pause on that, because I think that is a big question that's been hanging over all of this for those of us watching.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里停顿一下，因为我认为对于我们这些观察者来说，这是一个一直悬而未决的大问题。

sentences.en: Is this a prelude to what we saw in Venezuela, where Nicolas Maduro was indicted by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是否是我们所见过的委内瑞拉事件的前奏？当时尼古拉斯·马杜罗被美国

sentences.en: government and then was extracted by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 政府起诉，随后被美国

sentences.en: military?
sentences.zh: 军方抓捕？

sentences.en: Is that what this is about?
sentences.zh: 这就是这件事的意义吗？

sentences.en: It's very important to note that our reporting shows that President Trump wants the option.
sentences.zh: 非常重要的一点是，我们的报道显示特朗普总统想要这个选项。

sentences.en: He wants the option to do a military extraction to get Raul Castro to put pressure on the Cuban government.
sentences.zh: 他想要通过军事抓捕来带走劳尔·卡斯特罗，从而向古巴政府施压的选项。

sentences.en: You saw Todd Blanche raise that.
sentences.zh: 你看到托德·布兰奇提到了这一点。

sentences.en: He talked about how would they get Castro, right?
sentences.zh: 他谈到了他们将如何抓捕卡斯特罗，对吧？

sentences.en: And he talked about it being a Pentagon issue.
sentences.zh: 他还谈到这是一个五角大楼的问题。

sentences.en: That said, it's also important to note that there aren't a lot of special operations forces in the region.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，同样重要的是要注意到，该地区并没有太多的特种作战部队。

sentences.en: There aren't special operations forces that we know of that have been training for this kind of operation.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，并没有特种作战部队在为这种行动进行训练。

sentences.en: Cuba is very different than Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 古巴与委内瑞拉非常不同。

sentences.en: The circumstances are different.
sentences.zh: 情况也不同。

sentences.en: It seems that an actual military extraction of Castro is pretty remote.
sentences.zh: 看来实际对卡斯特罗进行军事抓捕的可能性相当渺茫。

sentences.en: You know, all the special operations forces are still in the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有的特种作战部队仍然在中东。

sentences.en: They're still geared up to possible action against Iran, right?
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在为可能针对伊朗的行动做准备，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to reset and come back for Cuba.
sentences.zh: 你必须重新部署并调回古巴。

sentences.en: And it wouldn't necessarily have the same effect.
sentences.zh: 而且这未必会产生同样的效果。

sentences.en: Like, Nicolas Maduro was the official president of Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 比如，尼古拉斯·马杜罗是委内瑞拉的正式总统。

sentences.en: Pulling him out triggered a change in leadership.
sentences.zh: 把他带走引发了领导层的更迭。

sentences.en: It allowed Vice President Delce Rodriguez to become the acting president, to take power.
sentences.zh: 这使得副总统德尔西·罗德里格斯能够成为代理总统，掌握权力。

sentences.en: Raul Castro is a very important figure in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 劳尔·卡斯特罗是古巴非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: He is very politically influential.
sentences.zh: 他在政治上非常有影响力。

sentences.en: But if you grabbed him, it wouldn't change any official leadership, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你抓了他，并不会改变任何官方领导层，对吧？

sentences.en: The Cuban government would continue on.
sentences.zh: 古巴政府会继续运作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Everybody formally in charge would remain formally in charge because they would still be in the country.
sentences.zh: 所有正式掌权的人都会继续掌权，因为他们仍然在国内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so when you talk to outside experts, it is that reason that in the end, they see this as a threat, as pressure,
sentences.zh: 所以当你与外部专家交谈时，正是因为这个原因，他们最终将此视为一种威胁，一种压力，

sentences.en: as a signal more than a sign of what is to come.
sentences.zh: 一种信号，而不是未来走向的预示。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If it's appropriately viewed as a threat, as a kind of chip in these negotiations, in this game of chicken that's happening, to what end?
sentences.zh: 如果这被恰当地视为一种威胁，作为这些谈判中的一种筹码，在这场正在发生的“胆小鬼博弈”中，目的是什么？

sentences.en: Like, what does the U.S.
sentences.zh: 比如，美国

sentences.en: actually want from Cuba?
sentences.zh: 到底想从古巴得到什么？

sentences.en: Is the goal really wholesale regime change?
sentences.zh: 目标真的是彻底的政权更迭吗？

sentences.en: They've been a little unclear in their public comments about this.
sentences.zh: 他们在公开评论中对此一直有些含糊其辞。

sentences.en: And certainly the Cuban government wants to know what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当然，古巴政府也想知道美国的

sentences.en: demands are.
sentences.zh: 要求是什么。

sentences.en: But we did, in recent days, start to get some answers.
sentences.zh: 但最近几天，我们确实开始得到一些答案。

sentences.en: John Ratcliffe, the CIA director, last week took a trip to Cuba, first Trump cabinet official to go down there.
sentences.zh: 中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫上周前往古巴，这是第一位前往那里的特朗普内阁官员。

sentences.en: He delivered a message to the grandson of Raul Castro, the interior minister, and the head of Cuba's intelligence services.
sentences.zh: 他向劳尔·卡斯特罗的孙子——现任内政部长兼古巴情报部门负责人——传达了一个信息。

sentences.en: And he talked vaguely about economic and political change, but he also said that Cuba can't be a platform for America's adversaries.
sentences.zh: 他含糊地谈到了经济和政治变革，但也表示古巴不能成为美国对手的平台。

sentences.en: And the Cubans knew exactly what he was talking about.
sentences.zh: 古巴人很清楚他在说什么。

sentences.en: That was a reference to the Chinese intelligence post and the Russian military posts that are on Cuba.
sentences.zh: 那是暗指在古巴的中国情报站和俄罗斯军事基地。

sentences.en: These are installations the Russians and the Chinese use to intercept communications inside the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些是俄罗斯和中国用来拦截美国境内通信的设施。

sentences.en: They are listening to Southcom.
sentences.zh: 他们在监听南方司令部。

sentences.en: They may be listening up at Central Command.
sentences.zh: 他们可能也在监听中央司令部。

sentences.en: These are very important military bases, and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常重要的军事基地，美国

sentences.en: wants them closed.
sentences.zh: 希望它们关闭。

sentences.en: And this is a concrete ask, and it is something the Cubans could do, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个具体的要求，也是古巴人可以做到的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a step that they could take.
sentences.zh: 这是他们可以采取的一步。

sentences.en: There is a path to reduce that intelligence collection there, to either close the base or limit the number of people there or kind of restrict it.
sentences.zh: 有一条途径可以减少那里的情报收集，要么关闭基地，要么限制那里的人数，或者进行某种限制。

sentences.en: Radcliffe basically told the Cubans, look, if you want to do a deal with us, you got to kick our adversaries out.
sentences.zh: 拉特克利夫基本上告诉古巴人，听着，如果你想和我们做交易，你就得把我们的对手赶走。

sentences.en: They're spying on us from your country.
sentences.zh: 他们正在你们的国家监视我们。

sentences.en: They have to go.
sentences.zh: 他们必须离开。

sentences.en: What else did he ask for?
sentences.zh: 他还要求了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the economic and political demands were a lot more vague, but we are getting a sense of the kinds of things the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，经济和政治要求要模糊得多，但我们正在了解美国

sentences.en: wants to see.
sentences.zh: 想要看到的事情。

sentences.en: And they range from more extreme to easier things to do.
sentences.zh: 它们涵盖了从更极端到更容易实现的事情。

sentences.en: But they start off with reducing the power of the military, industrial-backed conglomerate that controls a huge chunk of the Cuban economy.
sentences.zh: 但它们首先是从削弱控制古巴经济很大一部分的军工联合体的权力开始的。

sentences.en: It could mean pushing more pragmatic, less dogmatic politicians forward.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着推动更务实、不那么教条的政治人物上位。

sentences.en: And it also could be a step toward free elections, right?
sentences.zh: 这也可能是迈向自由选举的一步，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you could see the U.S.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以看到美国

sentences.en: pushing for elections at the local level to make those more meaningful.
sentences.zh: 推动地方层面的选举，使其更有意义。

sentences.en: And that would be a real win.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个真正的胜利。

sentences.en: It would not be regime change.
sentences.zh: 那不会是政权更迭。

sentences.en: It would not be a total change in communist rule, but it would be a meaningful step forward.
sentences.zh: 那不会是共产主义统治的彻底改变，但那将是向前迈出的有意义的一步。

sentences.en: And would one of the smaller, more incremental of those demands be seen as a real success by the Trump administration?
sentences.zh: 那么，特朗普政府会将这些要求中较小、较渐进的一项视为真正的成功吗？

sentences.en: I mean, in Venezuela, they had this trophy of Nicolas Maduro being brought to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在委内瑞拉，他们有尼古拉斯·马杜罗被带到美国这个“战利品”，

sentences.en: to theoretically face justice.
sentences.zh: 理论上是为了面对正义。

sentences.en: In this case, if they aren't going to extract Castro, and that's largely a symbolic move.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，如果他们不打算抓捕卡斯特罗，那这在很大程度上就是一个象征性的举动。

sentences.en: If the goal is really these more modest changes,
sentences.zh: 如果目标确实是这些更温和的变革，

sentences.en: you could see the administration running the risk of being seen as making a compromise with an authoritarian government in Cuba while allowing them to remain in power.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到政府面临一种风险，即被视为在与古巴的威权政府妥协，同时又任由他们继续掌权。

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: That is a very important point, and one that we can't lose sight of.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的观点，也是我们不能忽视的一点。

sentences.en: Inside the United States, there is a big constituency, an important constituency, an influential constituency for regime change in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 在美国国内，有一个庞大的、重要的、有影响力的选民群体支持古巴政权更迭。

sentences.en: Cuban Americans have wanted for years and years to end communist control of Cuba.
sentences.zh: 古巴裔美国人多年来一直希望结束古巴的共产主义统治。

sentences.en: Anything that is short of that is going to feel inadequate.
sentences.zh: 任何达不到这一点的做法都会让人觉得不够充分。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the Trump administration knows that sometimes when they reach for the big goal, they fall short.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，特朗普政府知道，有时当他们追求宏大目标时，往往会以失败告终。

sentences.en: And when they reach for the smaller, they can be more successful.
sentences.zh: 而当他们追求较小的目标时，反而更容易成功。

sentences.en: I assume when you're referring to reaching for a big and difficult-to-achieve goal, you're talking about Iran.
sentences.zh: 我假设当你提到追求宏大且难以实现的目标时，你指的是伊朗。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you remember, on the night of the Iran war this year, President Trump delivered a video address to the nation, and he talked expansively about war goals.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得，在今年伊朗战争的那天晚上，特朗普总统向全国发表了视频讲话，他广泛地谈到了战争目标。

sentences.en: He talked about regime change.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了政权更迭。

sentences.en: He called on the Iranian people to rise up.
sentences.zh: 他呼吁伊朗人民奋起反抗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And pushing for regime change is not a narrow mission.
sentences.zh: 推动政权更迭并不是一项狭窄的任务。

sentences.en: It is not something that is easy to achieve.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件容易实现的事情。

sentences.en: It's something that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是美国在一次又一次的战争中

sentences.en: has struggled with in war after war.
sentences.zh: 苦苦挣扎的事情。

sentences.en: They can do it, but it usually requires a very big ground force and unleashes forces that are out of anyone's control.
sentences.zh: 他们可以做到，但这通常需要非常庞大的地面部队，并会释放出任何人都无法控制的力量。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Iran is a mess.
sentences.zh: 伊朗现在是一团糟。

sentences.en: Like, they don't have a peace deal that's lasting yet.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们还没有达成持久的和平协议。

sentences.en: But they're contemplating starting strikes again.
sentences.zh: 但他们正在考虑重新开始打击行动。

sentences.en: The Supreme Leader has been killed, but the government is as hardline as ever.
sentences.zh: 最高领袖虽然已经被杀，但政府依然强硬如初。

sentences.en: They are not backing down from their nuclear program demands.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在核计划要求上做出让步。

sentences.en: And if you look at President Trump's other foreign military adventures, foreign operations,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看特朗普总统的其他对外军事冒险和海外行动，

sentences.en: they've been much more narrowly cast with a very specific goal to kill a specific leader, to bomb a specific nuclear site, or in the Venezuela case, to capture Nicolas Maduro.
sentences.zh: 它们的范围要狭窄得多，目标也非常明确，比如杀死某个特定的领导人、轰炸某个特定的核设施，或者在委内瑞拉的案例中，抓捕尼古拉斯·马杜罗。

sentences.en: When he has drawn the goals narrowly, he has seen more success.
sentences.zh: 当他把目标定得狭窄时，他看到了更多的成功。

sentences.en: And so, if you look at Cuba, the kind of long-term goal of many Cuban Americans of a Cuba free of communism, that's going to be harder to achieve.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你看看古巴，许多古巴裔美国人长期以来希望古巴摆脱共产主义的愿望，那将更难实现。

sentences.en: But if you look for more narrow goals, reduction of the power of the military industrial state, incremental steps toward elections, those are achievable things.
sentences.zh: 但如果你寻找更狭窄的目标，比如削弱军工体制的权力、朝着选举迈出渐进的步伐，这些都是可以实现的事情。

sentences.en: You could make meaningful progress.
sentences.zh: 你可以取得有意义的进展。

sentences.en: Even so, Julian, you more than anyone know that Cuba has been in the sights of the CIA for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，朱利安，你比任何人都清楚，古巴长期以来一直处于中情局的监视之下。

sentences.en: So, why would the administration take this on right now, given everything you're saying?
sentences.zh: 那么，考虑到你所说的一切，为什么政府现在要处理这个问题呢？

sentences.en: Given that the administration is already in the middle of a war in the Middle East, that people are already skeptical of what the administration is doing abroad?
sentences.zh: 考虑到政府已经深陷中东战争，人们已经对政府在海外的所作所为持怀疑态度？

sentences.en: Why do this now?
sentences.zh: 为什么要现在做这件事？

sentences.en: Well, as you just said, Cuba has been a thorn in America's side for decades and decades.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你刚才所说，几十年来，古巴一直是美国的一根刺。

sentences.en: This is not some adventure that came out of this administration's head, right?
sentences.zh: 这并不是本届政府头脑发热想出的什么冒险行动，对吧？

sentences.en: There have been generations of American leaders who have tried to change the government in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 几代美国领导人都曾试图改变古巴的政府。

sentences.en: It is something that is very important to a powerful constituency in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这对美国国内一个强大的选民群体来说非常重要。

sentences.en: And Trump sees himself as someone who can cut through bureaucracy, as someone who can solve problems that have bedeviled the United States for years.
sentences.zh: 特朗普把自己看作是一个能够打破官僚主义的人，一个能够解决困扰美国多年问题的人。

sentences.en: He's someone who has little patience for progress or history, who believes through the force of will he can fix them or change them.
sentences.zh: 他是一个对进步或历史缺乏耐心的人，他相信通过意志的力量就能修复或改变它们。

sentences.en: And also, we do have Iran right now, and Iran looks like a really difficult problem.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们现在确实有伊朗问题，伊朗看起来是一个非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, he's got Cuba, and his pressure campaign is working better than they thought.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他又有了古巴问题，而且他的施压运动比他们预想的要有效。

sentences.en: So, there's a sense here, among some in the administration, that Cuba could be the success that helps them move past the morass of Iran.
sentences.zh: 所以，政府内部有些人认为，古巴可能成为帮助他们走出伊朗泥潭的成功案例。

sentences.en: Trump may essentially just be looking for a win.
sentences.zh: 特朗普本质上可能只是在寻找一场胜利。

sentences.en: You're saying.
sentences.zh: 你是说。

sentences.en: If we know anything about Donald Trump, he's always looking for a win.
sentences.zh: 如果我们对唐纳德·特朗普有什么了解的话，那就是他总是在寻找一场胜利。

sentences.en: Well, Julian, thank you so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 好的，朱利安，非常感谢你来到节目中。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, two police officers who defended the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，两名在1月6日保卫美国

sentences.en: Capitol against a pro-Trump mob on January 6th challenged the constitutionality of a new $1.8 billion fund that they warned could reward those who participated in the attack.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦免受特朗普支持者暴徒袭击的警察，对一项新的18亿美元基金的合宪性提出了质疑，他们警告称该基金可能会奖励那些参与袭击的人。

sentences.en: Their lawsuit will answer the question of whether anyone has the legal standing to stop the Trump administration from creating the controversial fund.
sentences.zh: 他们的诉讼将回答一个问题，即是否有人具有法律地位来阻止特朗普政府设立这一有争议的基金。

sentences.en: That fund is expected to make payments to Trump supporters, including January 6th rioters, who claim their prosecutions were politically motivated.
sentences.zh: 该基金预计将向特朗普的支持者支付款项，包括那些声称自己受到政治迫害的1月6日骚乱者。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 还有。

sentences.en: What I realized was a lot of Americans were not homophobic, but thought they were supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 我意识到很多美国人并不是恐同，而是认为自己应该表现得恐同。

sentences.en: And as more of us came out and our reality confronted the prejudice, we made great gains.
sentences.zh: 随着我们越来越多的人出柜，我们的现实与偏见发生碰撞，我们取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: Barney Frank, the blunt-talking former congressman from Massachusetts,
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克，这位来自马萨诸塞州、说话直率的前国会议员，

sentences.en: who for decades was the most prominent gay politician in America and who wrote the most sweeping overhaul of U.S.
sentences.zh: 几十年来一直是美国最著名的同性恋政治家，并撰写了自大萧条以来美国最全面的

sentences.en: financial regulations since the Great Depression, has died.
sentences.zh: 金融监管改革法案，已经去世了。

sentences.en: He was 86.
sentences.zh: 他享年86岁。

sentences.en: His signature legislation, the Dodd-Frank Law, passed after the 2008 financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 他的标志性立法《多德-弗兰克法案》是在2008年金融危机后通过的。

sentences.en: It regulated derivatives that had worsened the crisis, imposed new rules on large banks, and created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau as an industry watchdog.
sentences.zh: 它监管了加剧危机的衍生品，对大银行实施了新规，并创建了消费者金融保护局作为行业监督机构。

sentences.en: Asked about complaints from business leaders about the law, Frank scoffed.
sentences.zh: 当被问及商界领袖对该法的抱怨时，弗兰克嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: Well, I hate to say this, but what I, the impression I get most is that their feelings are hurt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不想这么说，但我得到的最大印象是他们的感情受到了伤害。

sentences.en: Oh, you were rude to us.
sentences.zh: 哦，你对我们太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: You said we were fat cats.
sentences.zh: 你说我们是肥猫。

sentences.en: You hurt our feelings.
sentences.zh: 你伤害了我们的感情。

sentences.en: Get over it.
sentences.zh: 克服它吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm in the kind of business where people say rude things about us all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我从事的行业里，人们一直都在说关于我们的粗鲁言论。

sentences.en: I've said that to them.
sentences.zh: 我对他们也是这么说的。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Nowetsky and Diana Nguyen, with help from Lindsay Garrison.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由瑞奇·诺维茨基和戴安娜·阮制作，林赛·加里森提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Michael Benoit.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林和迈克尔·伯努瓦编辑。

sentences.en: Contains music by Aliciava Etoop, Marion Lozano, Pat McCusker, and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含艾丽西亚瓦·埃图普、马里昂·洛扎诺、帕特·麦卡斯克和丹·鲍威尔的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly创作。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由克里斯·伍德录制。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场痛苦、混乱，有时又令人激动的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，和我一起，莎拉·凯尼格，讲述那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的人们的故事。

sentences.zh: 《地铁》，在任何你获取播客的地方收听。

sentences.zh: 《地铁》，在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
